stem: To meet the criteria for a Brief Resolved Unexplained Event (BRUE), the episode must last for less than which duration and occur in a child of what age?

options.text: Less than $1$ minute in a child under $12$ months of age
Less than $2$ minutes in a child under $6$ months of age
Less than $1$ minute in a child under $2$ years of age
Less than $30$ seconds in a child under $2$ months of age

explanation: A BRUE is defined by its brief nature, typically lasting less than $60$ seconds, and is specific to infants under one year old.
rationale: Focus on the specific time limit and the age threshold that defines infancy in this clinical context.

optionExplanations.A: A BRUE is defined by its brief nature, typically lasting less than $60$ seconds, and is specific to infants under one year old.
optionExplanations.B: While many episodes are very short, the official diagnostic criteria extend the age limit to $12$ months and cap the duration at $1$ minute.
optionExplanations.C: The age limit for BRUE is strictly under $12$ months; events in older children are classified differently.
optionExplanations.D: Although infants under $2$ months are considered high risk, the general definition of a BRUE covers children up to $12$ months.
